scope: AI-chat claim evidence admission, citation integrity, source quality, freshness, contradiction, independence, and publication eligibility
invariants: citation proximity never establishes evidence authority
claim identity preserves polarity relation quantity unit and content anchors
citation binding must match source identity locator and content digest
citation binding must remain materially identical to the canonical claim
evidence tenant claim and scope bindings fail closed on mismatch
source quality is explicit policy-bound metadata rather than model inference
model-produced or generated-source evidence is never authoritative
current-evidence requirements reject stale or future observations
correlated copies cannot satisfy independent-origin requirements
authoritative contradiction yields a contested publication disposition
high and critical risk claims can require primary-source support and stronger independence
quarantined or rejected evidence cannot silently count toward support
publication eligibility receipts are deterministic and non-executing
backend citation and claim-identity modules are compatibility facades over one canonical verification implementation
final response acceptance requires explicit claim-to-receipt bindings and rejects missing stale contested abstained or mismatched required evidence

promotion.rule: implemented candidate only; exact-head structural validation, focused regressions, legacy citation regression compatibility, independent rehash, and AI-file-tree governance must pass before qualification
